raw_response:
I have farmed this land in Quzhou County for 40 years. I finished middle school, so I can read and do figures, but most of what I know comes from doing it year after year and watching what works in my village. My farm is 10.1 mu total. I keep about 7 mu for wheat and maize in rotation, and the other 3.1 mu for cotton. That is the same split as last year. I do not want to change too much because change is risky, and at my age I cannot afford a bad harvest.

For the winter wheat on 7 mu, I will plant an improved variety. Last year I used one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base dressing — that is 50 jin, about 25 kg of compound fertilizer. Then I top-dressed with urea twice, about 15 kg each time. This year fertilizer got more expensive, but I will still use the same amount because cutting back is not worth the risk. I figure that comes to about 16 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times: once before winter to protect the seedlings from freezing, once at jointing in spring, and once at heading. I spray pesticide twice, mainly for aphids and powdery mildew. I do rotary tillage before planting. If the weather holds, I expect about 480 kg per mu.

For summer maize on the same 7 mu, I plant a hybrid right after the wheat comes off in June. I do not do deep tillage — just direct seeding into the wheat stubble. It saves time and the stubble keeps the soil from drying out too fast. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 jin per mu, and then top dress with urea once when the plants are knee-high. That is about 15 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice if the rain does not come, especially when the ears are filling. Two sprays for corn borers. I expect around 550 kg per mu.

For cotton on 3.1 mu, I plant a hybrid in late April. Cotton needs loose soil, so I do rotary tillage and make the beds well. I use about 13 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu — I put more potassium than on the grain crops because the input dealer told me cotton uses a lot for the bolls, and I saw that my neighbor Li's cotton did better last year when he used more potassium. I irrigate three times and spray four times. Cotton pests never stop, so you have to stay on it. I hope for 260 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I think about money every time I buy inputs. Fertilizer and pesticide prices have gone up again. But I always tell myself: a bad harvest is a disaster, wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost. So I stick close to what I did last year, maybe a touch more rather than less. With just me and my wife working 10.1 mu, we have to be careful with labor too. That is why I do no-tillage for maize — we cannot do everything by hand anymore.
